meta.title: Housing tax credit basis, fee, credit-limit and underwriting rules
meta.review_reason: CHFA adopts a new Qualified Allocation Plan every two years; the 2027-2028 plan replaces S1 for applications from 2027.
meta.scope: Rules the Deal Calculator applies to itemized development costs: grant treatment, the 30% basis boost, the applicable fraction, CHFA's contractor and developer fee limits, CHFA's per-project credit limits, CHFA's minimum and high debt-coverage thresholds, the tax-exempt bond aggregate basis test for 4% credits, CHFA's minimum operating reserve, and CHFA's review of deferred developer fee repayment from cash flow.
meta.methodology: Every value is copied from the statute, regulation or CHFA plan it cites, with a verbatim quote and its location. A rule whose status is adopted and whose source exists is applied. A draft value is shown beside the adopted one and never applied. A rule with no source is shown as rule not sourced and is not applied.

status_values.adopted: In force for the stated period; the calculator applies it.
status_values.draft: Proposed but not adopted; shown separately and not applied.

meta.not_included: CHFA's cost basis limits (Method Three, published only in the Excel application), the state credit three-test calculation, HUD subsidy layering limits, CHFA's discretionary developer-fee increase for special populations, CHFA's minimum rehabilitation hard costs, and CHFA's discretion to award less credit than the calculated amount.

S1.title: CHFA 2025-2026 Qualified Allocation Plan, Second Amendment
S1.version: Adopted by the CHFA Board 2025-09-26; approved by the Governor 2025-11-13

S3.title: 26 CFR 1.42-16, Eligible basis reduced by federal grants

grant_basis_treatment.quote: The eligible basis of a building shall not include any costs financed with the proceeds of a federally funded grant.

also_quote.quote: any portion of the grant is funded with federal funds (whether or not includible in gross income)

federal_grant.note: A grant funded in whole or in part with federal money, including federal money a state or city passes through as a grant (HOME, CDBG, NHTF, Capital Magnet Fund).

federal_loan.note: The statute reduces basis for grants only; federal money lent to the project is a loan, not a grant.

nonfederal_grant.note: A grant with no federal money in it (for example state Proposition 123 or local general funds) is not a federally funded grant.

applicable_fraction.quote: The term "applicable fraction" means the smaller of the unit fraction or the floor space fraction

acquisition_credit_rate.quote: For competitive acquisition Housing Tax Credits, the APR floor is set at 4 percent.
acquisition_credit_rate.method_quote: Qualified acquisition costs multiplied by applicable percentage rate equals annual Housing Tax Credit amount
acquisition_credit_rate.note: A floor: the calculator has no input for the applicable acquisition percentage, so it applies the floor and labels it as the floor.

credit_reservation_methods.quote: The amount of Housing Tax Credits reserved will be based on the smallest of the amounts resulting from these calculation methods.
credit_reservation_methods.gap_quote: Gap divided by Housing Tax Credit equity factor divided by 10 years equals annual Federal Credit amount
credit_reservation_methods.gap_sources_quote: Total uses of funds minus total sources (excluding equity from the sale of Housing Tax Credits) of funds equals gap (equity needed from Housing Tax Credits)
credit_reservation_methods.cost_basis_limit_reason: CHFA lists its cost basis limits (Method Three) only in the Excel application, so the calculator does not check them.

basis_boost.quote: The Code allows for a 30 percent basis boost for projects located in one of the following areas

sadda.label: HUD Small Area Difficult Development Area

chfa.label: CHFA basis boost (state designation)
chfa.quote: The CHFA basis boost only applies to new construction and rehabilitation eligible basis of federal 9 percent Housing Tax Credit projects.
chfa.up_to_quote: CHFA is authorized to award up to a 30-percent “basis boost” to buildings that it determines need the boost to be economically feasible.

basis_boost.acquisition_quote: The basis boost options above do not apply to acquisition basis.

statute.quote: Any building which is designated by the State housing credit agency as requiring the increase in credit

contractor_fee_limit.quote: Aggregate Builder's Profit, Overhead* as a Percent of Hard Construction Costs
contractor_fee_limit.base: New structures or rehabilitation, onsite work, contingency and accessory structures

developer_fee_limit.quote: Aggregate Developer Fee and Consultant Fee* Limits as a Percent of Certain Project Costs
developer_fee_limit.tested_on: Developer fee plus consultant fee, before any deferral
base_subtracts: 50% of acquisition, except for projects serving people experiencing homelessness or special populations
developer_fee_limit.base_quote: Calculated by subtracting the following costs from the total project costs and applying the allowable percentage rate from the table below

special_population_increase.reason: CHFA must approve the increase; it is prorated by the share of units serving people experiencing homelessness or special populations at or below 30% AMI.

developer_fee_limit.acquisition_exception_quote: Fifty percent of Acquisition cost (excluding projects serving Persons experiencing Homelessness or Special Populations)

credit_cap_federal_9pct.quote: CHFA will accept Applications for no more than $1,800,000 of the annual federal 9 percent Housing Tax Credit for any one project or any one Applicant

credit_cap_state_with_9pct.quote: CHFA will pair, if requested, a fixed amount of $500,000 of standard annual state credit with federal 9 percent Housing Tax Credit Applications.

credit_cap_state_round_two_accelerated.quote: CHFA will accept Applications for $1,300,000 of accelerated annual state credit and will pair up to $600,000 of standard annual state credit for any one project or any one Applicant, or Affiliate of such Applicant, or Turn-key Project Developer of such Applicant in Round Two.

credit_cap_state_round_two_standard.quote: CHFA will accept Applications for $1,300,000 of accelerated annual state credit and will pair up to $600,000 of standard annual state credit for any one project or any one Applicant, or Affiliate of such Applicant, or Turn-key Project Developer of such Applicant in Round Two.

credit_cap_state_with_4pct.quote: CHFA will accept Applications for $10,000 per unit of standard or accelerated annual state credit up to $700,000 maximum per Application, as available, for any one project or any one Applicant or Affiliate of such Applicant applying for projects financed with tax-exempt Private Activity Bonds and federal 4 percent Housing Tax Credits in September, October, and November 2025 and 2026.

state_credit_term.quote: The APR for new construction and rehabilitation with the total six-year allocation of state credits is 30 percent of Qualified Basis.

min_debt_coverage.quote: Minimum 1.15 to 1.0 for all amortized debt throughout the initial 15-year pro forma period.

high_coverage_credit_reduction.quote: At the time of application, projects with debt coverage ratios that exceed 1.3 to 1.0 may be eligible for less Housing Tax Credit than the amount calculated
high_coverage_credit_reduction.effect: CHFA may award less credit; the amount is at CHFA's discretion, so the calculator flags it and does not reduce the credit.

pro_forma_vacancy.location: Section 4.C, Minimum Pro Forma Underwriting Assumptions, item 1
pro_forma_vacancy.quote: Seven percent on all project income, 10 percent vacancy rate for any retail/commercial income, five percent for any projects receiving a project-based Section 8 subsidy for 100 percent of the units.

pro_forma_rent_growth.location: Section 4.C, Minimum Pro Forma Underwriting Assumptions, item 2
pro_forma_rent_growth.quote: Annual Rental Income Growth Two percent

pro_forma_expense_growth.location: Section 4.C, Minimum Pro Forma Underwriting Assumptions, item 3
pro_forma_expense_growth.quote: Annual Operating Expense Growth Three percent

pupa_minimum.location: Section 4.C, Minimum Pro Forma Underwriting Assumptions, item 4
pupa_minimum.quote: $4,500 excluding replacement reserves, higher for projects that are providing additional services, and $5,000 for project-based Section 8 projects.

replacement_reserve_minimum.quote: Minimum replacement reserves must equal $300/unit annually for senior projects and $350/unit annually for family projects.

bond_aggregate_basis_test.quote: 25 percent or more of the aggregate basis of such building and the land on which the building is located is financed by 1 or more obligations described in subparagraph (A)

also_quote.quote: 50 percent or more of the aggregate basis of such building and the land on which the building is located is financed by 1 or more obligations described in subparagraph (A)

bond_aggregate_basis_test.post_2025_quote: are part of an issue the issue date of which is after December 31, 2025, and provide the financing for not less than 5 percent of the aggregate basis of such building and the land on which the building is located
bond_aggregate_basis_test.effective_quote: The amendment made by this subsection shall apply to buildings placed in service in taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025.

chfa_quote.quote: Housing Tax Credits are allowed for that portion of a project’s eligible basis that is financed with the tax-exempt bonds. The project may be entitled to Housing Tax Credits for up to the full amount of qualified basis when meeting the aggregate basis test.

bond_aggregate_basis_test.basis: aggregate basis of the building and the land on which it is located

operating_reserve_minimum.quote: The total project budget must include minimum operating reserves equal to at least four months of projected annual operating expenses and four months of debt service payments, although CHFA may require an increased operating reserve based on lease-up projections contained in the Market Study.

deferred_fee_repayment_review.quote: Throughout the 15-year pro forma period, CHFA will also consider such items as debt coverage ratios, the ability to pay deferred developer fees from cash flows, operating reserve amounts, and annual operating expenses.
deferred_fee_repayment_review.kind: review item, not a numeric limit
